findings.claim: The target-framework guard disables the feature on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on those targets. Consequently, generated code on those supported targets remains coverage-instrumented, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated except where the attribute cannot be emitted. The README's claim that these targets lack the attribute is also incorrect.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator with NetStandard20 reference assemblies and parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0. First assert that compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute") is non-null, proving the attribute is available; then inspect active attributes on every generated class and assert ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is present. This fails on head because all occurrences of `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` exclude it. Repeat with .NET Framework reference assemblies and NETFRAMEWORK defined.

findings.claim: The copy operation in MessagePackSecurity no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. A copy of a security configuration can therefore silently retain the destination's previous collision-resistance setting instead of the source's, potentially dropping hash-collision protection; this is an unrelated behavioral and security regression in a coverage-only change.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a unit test that creates a source MessagePackSecurity with HashCollisionResistant = true, performs the copy operation containing this hunk on a destination with HashCollisionResistant = false, and asserts the destination value is true. Also test propagation in the opposite direction. The first case fails after the removed assignment.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The implemented reading: every generator-emitted formatter, resolver, and private helper/cache class is decorated unconditionally wherever the attribute is considered available, with no new setting.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: A narrower, configurable reading: only the formatter and resolver types themselves require decoration, helper/cache classes need not have it, and users may opt out through a GeneratorOptions setting. This would remove the helper-class attributes and gate all attribute emission on that opt-out.
